problem.text: model_diff.py loaded tensors directly and retained collection file handles across module comparisons, despite unloading each module.

reasoning.text: The change brackets each model's module.load with begin_deferred_load/end_deferred_load, then closes that model's collection after forwarding and unloading. Completing deferred reads before forwarding is essential because deferred get_tensor returns allocated destinations before filling them.

impact.text: The normal comparison path now batches eligible tensor reads within each module and releases file handles between modules; comparison formulas and device selection remain unchanged.

source_notes.text: The root usage-evaluation entry establishes the original module-at-a-time diagnostic. The later metrics entry records the final-logit diagnostics and a vocabulary-versus-sequence bound observation.

PR #26, “Superior 3INST parameters,” proposes decoder changes; its discussion includes turboderp announcing KLD evaluation in model_diff.py. Its relationship to this loading change is inferred only from the shared script, not an explicit commit link or a reported loading failure.

limitations: No model inference, native loader execution, file-handle measurement or throughput benchmark was performed.
The scalar check models inherited perplexity indexing only; it does not establish Torch behavior on empty slices or numerical metric values.
The added cleanup is on the normal path, not protected by exception-handling cleanup.

chapters.title: Module-scoped deferred loading and handle cleanup

claims.text: Both A and B follow the same sequence: begin deferred loading, load the module, finish deferred loading, prepare and forward activations, unload, close collection handles, then free memory. A finishes this sequence before B begins.

Deferral applies to the default mt_fread backend unless get_tensor requests no_defer. The Python backend remains immediate. end_deferred_load groups requests by file and CPU/CUDA destination, sorts by decreasing byte size, dispatches chunked native workloads, performs required temporary-to-destination copies, and clears deferred state.

close closes nonempty native handles and resets their slots to None without discarding tensor metadata. Later loads can reopen the same files. This trades persistent handle reuse for module-bounded handle retention; any speed or resource benefit remains an inference rather than a measurement.
The earlier perplexity bound observation carries over unchanged: this diff does not alter the nested ppl helper or its caller.

findings.description: The unchanged perplexity helper bounds sequence-axis slicing by vocabulary size.
findings.trigger: Prediction-position count exceeds vocabulary size; larger vocabularies instead cause trailing empty slices.
findings.expected_behavior: Accumulate every next-token prediction exactly once.
findings.actual_behavior: For 2047 prediction positions and vocabulary size 1024, only 1024 positions are included. The direct caller is main's per-model final-logit loop, reachable through this script's CLI.

verification.description: Whole-parent-tree search located the nested helper and its direct caller. Inspection shows shape[1] controlling slices along axis zero; the task leaves both unchanged.
verification.limits: Literal search does not establish external or dynamic callers.

verification.description: A standard-library model counted 1024 positions in one pass for vocabulary 1024, and all 2047 positions in four passes for vocabulary 32000.
verification.limits: Models integer bounds only; does not execute the repository helper or Torch.

annotation.summary: Uses deferred tensor loading and closes file handles after each compared module, without changing comparison metrics; an inherited perplexity indexing issue remains.
